title: I’M NOT GOOD ENOUGH.
paragraphs: I’M NOT GOOD ENOUGH.
The deliverer of Israel had a speech issue.
You think your weakness disqualifies you?
Let me take you to a desert.

Sand in the wind.
A bush on fire — but not burning.
And a shepherd with trembling lips.
In Book of Exodus 4, Moses finally says what he’s been thinking all along:
“Lord… I’m not eloquent. I am slow of speech and tongue.”
Translation?

I can’t do this.
I’m not built for this.
Send someone else.

The man who would stand before Pharaoh…
The man who would stretch out his hand over the Red Sea…
The man whose face would shine with glory…
He stuttered.
Or at least he believed he did.
And here’s the open wound we don’t like to touch:

God had already called him.
Already chosen him.
Already promised, “I will be with you.”
But Moses was still arguing.
Why?
Because insecurity feels safer than obedience.
Listen carefully.

Moses wasn’t just doubting his speech.
He was doubting the One who made his mouth.
And then God answers with thunder wrapped in tenderness:
“Who made man’s mouth? … Is it not I, the Lord?”
Feel that.

Your weakness?
Not a surprise to God.
Not an oversight.
Not a flaw in His design.
It’s the stage.

We love polished leaders.
God loves surrendered ones.
Here’s the tension — and don’t miss this.

Moses’ insecurity didn’t disqualify him.
But his refusal almost did.
“Please send someone else.”

That wasn’t humility anymore.
That was resistance.
Some scholars interpret Moses’ “slow of speech” as a literal speech impediment. Others see it as lack of confidence or rhetorical training. Either way, the point stands:

God knew.
And He still called him.
Let me come close.
What excuse are you hiding behind?

“I’m too broken.”
“I’m not educated.”
“I failed before.”
“I don’t speak well.”
“I’m not spiritual enough.”

Beloved… that’s not humility.
That’s fear dressed in logic.

The Gospel doesn’t begin with your adequacy.
It begins with your surrender.

Moses needed Aaron.
Yes.
But you know what Moses needed more?
Presence.
And that’s what you and I have in fullness through Jesus Christ.

Where Moses had a staff,
we have a cross.

Where Moses had a burning bush,
we have an empty tomb.
The greater Deliverer has already come.

Gospel of Matthew 28:20 —
“I am with you always.”

Same promise.
Greater covenant.

Your insecurity is loud.
But Christ is louder.

Your weakness is real.
But His grace is stronger.
You are not good enough.
And that’s the point.
Because the story was never about your strength.
It’s about a holy God who uses trembling vessels to display unstoppable glory.
Stop negotiating with your calling.

Repent of hiding.
Lay down the excuse.
Say yes — even with shaking hands.
